title: These clever apps show off the iPhone Duo’s potential
title_bn: এই স্মার্ট অ্যাপগুলো আইফোন ডুও এর সম্ভাব্যতা দেখায়
author: TechPulse
excerpt: From retro cassette players and virtual notebooks to flight trackers and even a digital toaster, developers are finding creative ways to take advantage of Apple's first foldable iPhone.
paragraph1: It’s been a long time since I’ve been genuinely excited about a new iPhone. For years, a new iPhone meant a device that was thinner, faster, and had a camera that came with incredible upgrades. At some point (and Apple devotees can debate which year’s model this was!), a new iPhone became an incremental upgrade. Slightly better, slightly faster. Maybe there was a new button to learn, a new charging cable, or a new notch on the screen, but the iPhone itself remained the same rectangular glass and metal handheld it always was. The iPhone Duo changes this, allowing Apple to enter the market for foldable phones with a phone that, while imperfect, is whimsical, fun, and, yes, actually exciting. Image Credits:Apple It’s hard to say when the urge to acquire the iPhone Duo first kicked in. I’ll admit that it wasn’t during the official announcement, which left me feeling puzzled about the device’s potential. Do I actually want a phone that folds, I wondered? Was propping up the phone as a little tent to watch Netflix worth all that extra money? (The Duo starts at $2,000). As it turned out, the desire for the Duo grew on me as I saw developers embracing the new foldable design to create Duo-optimized apps.
paragraph2: Apple’s software development community, after all, is what keeps me locked into the iPhone. Apple developers are active, creative, engaged, and still often build for iOS first – a must if you like trying things early. Of course, the initial Duo reviews have pointed out how many mainstream iOS apps have not yet been made ready for the Duo, which is true. Many of the apps you use every day were not optimized by launch day, meaning they’re surrounded by black bars, have their controls in odd places, or have to be enlarged with a tap, similar to the early days of running iPhone apps on iPad. But the developers who have specifically built for the Duo sparked my interest. Soon, my inbox was filled with pitches for clever apps I couldn’t yet try unless I got my hands on a Duo. Hello, FOMO. The best of these don’t just adapt their apps to display correctly on the foldable form factor, but make use of the fact that there are different displays of different sizes – and they incorporate that into the design of the apps themselves. Below are some of my early favorites, tested on a review unit provided by Apple. Netflix Image Credits:Apple Let’s start with the basics. Netflix is one of Apple’s hand-picked partners for the Duo launch, and had its streaming app Duo-optimized by the time the device shipped, alongside others like the MLB app, NYT Cooking, Slack, my preferred calendar app Fantastical, and others. But Netflix is the perfect showcase for what I expect will be a regular Duo use case: watching movies and TV. The streaming app hasn’t just been expanded to fill the screen; it takes advantage of the fact that there are two different screen sizes to build for.
paragraph3: On the outer screen (the display you see when the device is folded), you can scroll through Netflix’s short-form, TikTok-like “Clips,” then open up the device to continue watching videos on the larger matte-screen inner display. The transition between the two experiences feels as seamless as unfolding the Duo itself, as the content automatically adapts to the new screen size. As I personally find myself watching most TV on my phone these days, as opposed to big screen in the living room, I appreciate having the option to shift from a phone to a larger screen with one device. This is going to be one of my most-used apps, I think. Deck-Man (Formerly Duo-Man) Image Credits:Deck-Man Look, I called it back in September. I have to credit Deck-Man, which was previously known as Duo-Man, as being the first app that made me want to get a Duo. Designed by indie developer Vidit Bhargava at a hackathon, the music player takes clever advantage of the Duo’s two screens to imitate how Walkman cassette players used to function. The playful app reimagines the cassette player as a digital experience with retro vibes, allowing you to browse through your favorite albums as cassettes, then load them into the player. You can then control the playback with play, pause, fast-forward, and rewind controls, as you would on a hardware device, complete with authentic-sounding clicks and cassette sounds that were recorded from a real portable cassette player. Image Credits:Deck-Man With the Duo open, the cassette appears to play on the right side of the screen, next to album imagery on the right. When closed, Deck-Man’s interface looks like the front of a Walkman. The app has appeal not only because it built something that could only exist on a hinged, foldable device like the Duo, but also because it taps into the growing demand for retro tech, which is partly a cultural response to the speed at which the AI industry is shipping out products. Retro tech, like dumbphones, digital cameras, vinyl, CDs, and landlines, recalls an older time when tech use was intentional, not just baked into every aspect of our lives.
paragraph4: Honestly, if you buy a Duo and don’t install Deck-Man, I’m convinced you just don’t know how to have fun. Duo-Man is now Deck-Man!Expanding my app to have a unique experience on all platforms and not just the Duo, so it only makes sense to have a better name reflecting that.See you October 23 on the App Store! pic.twitter.com/kCdjcmbeGG— Vidit Bhargava (@viditb) October 14, 2026 TypeDraw Image Credits:TypeDraw The TypeDraw app is designed to be a personal notebook, something that looks like a virtual Moleskine of sorts — it even has an elastic closure band. But there’s a certain charm to using this app specifically on the Duo, whose form factor makes it look a lot like a little notebook when closed. Inside TypeDraw, you can type using a font that’s your own handwriting or pick from one of a dozen fonts designed by its creator, Phil Traut. Image Credits:TypeDraw You can also choose which kind of paper you want to write on, like lined, grid, or dotted pages, and pick your ink color. You can also draw and sketch to create colorful images that accompany your handwritten text, which makes it feel a lot more like using a real-life notebook as your journal or diary, and not some boring to-do app. The pages curl as you flip through them, and you can even pull on the elastic band to produce a twang animation that’s just silly and fun. I turned iPhone Duo into a real-life notebook where you can type anywhere in your own handwriting or with one of 12 fonts I designed myself.
paragraph5: Type or draw, then close it. The next time you open the book, it shows your most recent note or the one captured nearest to your current… pic.twitter.com/d23kMbj8TH— Phil Traut ᯅ (@SpatiallyMe) October 15, 2026 Wakeout Wakeout, the workout app that’s a former Apple App of the Year winner, has also approached its Duo optimization thoughtfully by designing different user interfaces for each postion the phone can be in. The app, which offers a series of mini movement breaks that feel more like games than exercise, works when the Duo is closed, open, in tent mode, or sitting open like a laptop computer. Image Credits:Wakeout For instance, when the Duo is open like a book, the view is split across the hinge with the movement game videos on the left, but when it’s open like a laptop, the videos shift to the vertical screen. You can also put it into tent mode, which is great for watching the videos with the Duo propped up on your desk. (Most people use Wakeout at work, when they take quick stretch breaks after sitting at a desk for too long.) If the app is running on a closed Duo, its row of navigation tabs becomes a slim side menu in the column beside the camera, allowing the phone’s small screen to use the full display.

title: LG’s brilliant C6 OLED TV is already $400 off ahead of Black Friday
title_bn: LG’s brilliant C6 OLED TV is already $400 off ahead of Black Friday
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Black Friday is still over a month away, but if you’re hoping to upgrade your TV, you don’t need to wait until November. LG has already kicked off its early Black Friday sale, letting you save on the LG C6 and various soundbars through November
paragraph1: Black Friday is still over a month away, but if you’re hoping to upgrade your TV, you don’t need to wait until November. LG has already kicked off its early Black Friday sale, letting you save on the LG C6 and various soundbars through November 1st. Right now, for instance, you can snag a 55-inch C6 for an all-time low of $999.99 ($400 off), with Amazon and Best Buy matching said price.
paragraph2: Other sizes are also discounted, including the 65-inch model, which is on sale for $1,399.99 ($300 off) from Amazon, Best Buy, and LG. If you purchase direct, you’ll also get a free Xbox Wireless Controller and a complimentary wall mount.$1000LG’s C6 OLED TV offers a few small but welcome upgrades over last year’s C5, including a faster Alpha 11 AI Gen3 processor designed to improve picture and sound quality, along with a brighter display.
paragraph3: It also boasts a higher refresh rate of up to 165Hz for smoother gaming, up from 144Hz, while retaining four HDMI 2.1 ports and support for AMD FreeSync Premium and Nvidia G-Sync, the latter of which helps reduce unwanted screen tearing while gaming.Unsurprisingly, the C6 delivers the hallmarks of OLED technology, including inky blacks, vibrant color, and impressive contrast. Support for Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos, meanwhile, helps make movies and shows appear more lifelike and immersive, while built-in access to Netflix, HBO Max, and the like lets you stream your favorite content without a dedicated streaming device.
paragraph4: Google Cast and Apple AirPlay 2 also make it easy to share content from your phone, while Matter support lets you pair it with various smart home devices.Solid specs aside, we’d be remiss not to mention that researchers recently raised concerns about how LG’s smart TVs collect and log user data. LG has since responded to some of the accusations, saying its TVs don’t continuously record conversations, and that features like voice recognition and interest-based advertising are optional and disabled by default. While LG hasn’t addressed all concerns, similar data-collection practices aren’t necessarily unique to LG TVs, and they don’t detract from the C6’s impressive feature set.

title: The Boox Palma 2 Pro finally got me to stop reading on my phone
title_bn: The Boox Palma 2 Pro finally got me to stop reading on my phone
author: TechPulse
excerpt: The $400 Boox Palma 2 Pro is a smartphone-sized e-reader designed for people who want to read books, articles, and documents on a small E Ink display.
paragraph1: The $400 Boox Palma 2 Pro is a smartphone-sized e-reader designed for people who want to read books, articles, and documents on a small E Ink display. However, it offers more than just a dedicated reading experience because it runs Android and supports Google Play, giving you access to third-party apps. Think of it as a cross between a Kindle and a compact Android tablet. What drew me to reviewing the Palma 2 Pro was its size. When I’m not reading a physical book, I like to lie on my side and read at night before bed. Most e-readers are squarish and hard to hold without something like a PopSocket, and they can feel too big for reading while lying down. So even though I own a Kindle, I often ended up reading on my iPhone simply because it was more comfortable in my hand. But, reading on your phone for too long can of course cause eye strain. The Palma 2 Pro ultimately solved this problem for me during the two months I spent testing it.
paragraph2: The device’s front-lit screen lets you choose between cool and warm lighting. This was a big plus for me because when I’m reading in bed at night, I don’t want to disturb my sleeping husband with the light. While you can lower the brightness on a smartphone, the Palma 2 Pro can be dimmed to an exceptionally low level. Even when reading in complete darkness, I could see the screen clearly without straining my eyes or disturbing my husband. Not only was the Boox Palma 2 Pro easier on my eyes, but it was also noticeably lighter than my iPhone, weighing just 175 grams and making it even more comfortable to hold. Image Credits:Boox / And since it’s pocket-sized, I ended up carrying it everywhere, from the doctor’s office to the airport, especially since it fits in my small, everyday purse that isn’t big enough for a Kindle. So, in moments when I would normally scroll on my phone, I was getting some reading in instead. Since it’s not a locked-down e-reader, you can download apps like Kindle, Kobo, and Libby, as well as apps for audiobooks, podcasts, read-it-later services, and email. This means that you don’t have to use the built-in reader app, and can choose to read on your preferred app.
paragraph3: Access to apps turns the compact E Ink device into a versatile tool for reading, research, and productivity. It’s worth noting that while scrolling through these apps, animations and some interfaces may feel sluggish because not all apps are optimized for E Ink. And while the device is capable of displaying color, images will definitely look less vibrant than they would a smartphone screen. For me, the Palma 2 Pro became a dedicated device for reading and listening to audiobooks, which allowed me to enjoy the best of both worlds without the usual distractions that come with a smartphone. The Boox Palma 2 Pro also features a rear camera for scanning documents, a built-in speaker for listening to audio without headphones, and a hybrid SIM slot for cellular data on the go. Image Credits:Boox / The device is compatible with a stylus, so you can take notes and mark up PDFs. However, I can’t speak to that experience since I didn’t receive a stylus with my review unit. As for battery life, the device lasted about 5–7 days, which worked for me but could be a downside for people who are used to Kindles, which can last for weeks on a single charge. Additionally, if you want to get more juice out of the device, you can just turn off Wi-Fi.
paragraph4: One downside I found, especially for an e-reader at this price point, is that there’s quite a bit of ghosting. Text from a previous page can linger on the screen when you turn to the next page or return to the home screen. There’s a refresh button in the navigation bar that quickly clears it, but it may get annoying for some users to repeatedly have to do that. I think the Boox Palma 2 Pro is a great device for a very specific type of reader: someone who wants a smartphone-sized device for comfort, portability, as well as access to apps. If you’re someone who loves your Kindle, I don’t think this device is for you. But if, like me, you’re tired of reading on your phone and dealing with eye strain or headaches, the Boox Palma 2 Pro is a great option. Of course, the price is quite steep for an e-reader, so you’ll have to decide whether the added versatility and portability are worth the extra cost. It’s worth mentioning that Boox is launching a non-Pro Palma 3 soon for $340 that features a black and white display and replaces the Palma 2. title: What to expect from Apple’s ‘Pro and tell’ event
title_bn: অ্যাপলের প্রো এবং tell ইভেন্ট থেকে কি আশা করা যায়?
author: TechPulse
excerpt: It feels like Apple's Welcome Home event just happened. And the iPhone Duo announcement isn't all that far in our rearview mirror, either. Yet, the company is back with another launch, focused on the MacBook Pro, it looks like. Its "Pro and tell" eve
paragraph1: It feels like Apple’s Welcome Home event just happened. And the iPhone Duo announcement isn’t all that far in our rearview mirror, either. Yet, the company is back with another launch, focused on the MacBook Pro, it looks like. Its “Pro and tell” event is scheduled for October 28th at 1PM ET in Los Angeles. While obviously nothing is confirmed yet, it sure seems like we’re finally going to get that long-rumored touchscreen MacBook Pro.Beyond that? There could be an OLED update for the iPad Mini, plus M6 updates across other devices, following the M6 debut with the Mac Mini in August.
paragraph2: A touchscreen MacBook ProA MacBook Pro with an OLED touchscreen has been a fixture of the rumor mill since at least early 2023. But now, in late 2026, it may finally come to fruition. The name MacBook Ultra has been floating around, but Apple is unlikely to rebrand its flagship laptop line.This will be the first touchscreen laptop and the first OLED laptop from Apple. It will supposedly feature an iPhone-esque Dynamic Island, but don’t expect a dramatic revamp of the macOS interface — The touchscreen MacBook isn’t going to be some sort of iPad hybrid. It may include a few flourishes, like a magnification effect when you touch the screen or new gesture controls in native apps. But that’s it.
paragraph3: It’s also going to stick with the M5 series of chips for the time being — specifically, the M5 Pro and M5 Max. There might not be an M6 Pro or Max, even. Instead, Apple may wait to upgrade its higher-end processors until it introduces the M7 next year.M6 MacBook ProThat doesn’t mean there won’t be an M6 MacBook Pro, however. The base model of the MacBook Pro could be getting a bump from the M5 after the M6 debuted in the Mac Mini earlier this year. It might also get a slight redesign, including a hole-punch style camera. Unfortunately, they’re also expected to come with a price increase as component shortages reverberate through the Apple lineup.
paragraph4: M6 iMacThe iMac is also expected to get an M6 update, nearly two years after its last revision. Apple’s all-in-one desktop appears like it’s going to skip right over the M5. Don’t expect any real changes beyond that, though. But at least we might get some new color options, just like we did with the M4 model.OLED iPad MiniAnother long-rumored device that might finally be making its debut on Wednesday is the OLED iPad Mini. Other than the iPad Pro, the tablet lineup has stuck with LCDs until now. The new OLED iPad could kick off a broader transition for the product line.
paragraph5: The screen upgrade may add $100 to the cost, though. Otherwise, it likely won’t be a significant redesign, but expect a processor upgrade from the aging A17 to the A20 that debuted with the iPhone 18.Follow topics and authors from this story to see more like this in your personalized homepage feed and to receive email updates.

title: Here are the top AI agents that can live in your text messages
title_bn: Here are the top AI agents that can live in your text messages
author: TechPulse
excerpt: We created a list of the most notable AI agents that can live in your text messages, from general assistants to agents designed for families, travel, and work.
paragraph1: Rather than downloading another app, a growing number of agents can simply be texted like an ordinary person. You text it what you need, and it can remember context, connect to the apps and services you already use, and complete tasks on your behalf. That can mean scheduling an appointment, organizing a calendar, researching a trip, sending an email, making a reservation, shopping online, or reminding you about something days later. While Instinct is one of the buzziest AI agents at present, thanks to its $10 billion valuation after its latest funding round of $1 billion, there are many others also making a play for this space. Below are the most notable options so far, from general-purpose personal assistants to agents designed for families, travel, and work. Ask Proxy Image Credits:Ask Proxy Ask Proxy’s biggest differentiator is that it “thinks like a woman,” meaning it aims to anticipate your needs before you even ask, the company explains on its website. It works like a chatbot you can text like a friend, whether you need gift ideas, help planning an event, or recommendations for things to do that weekend. You can ask it to add important dates to your calendar, set reminders, or help with everyday decisions. You can also send it photos, like an empty table, to figure out how to decorate the table for a dinner party. Unlike a typical chatbot, Ask Proxy also takes a proactive approach. It can reach out when it notices something you might forget or when it comes across a new activity, restaurant, or experience you might enjoy. There’s also a work-focused version, which the company explains “gets employees back to work faster, while keeping personal data off company systems.” The personal version costs $1 per day. For businesses, pricing starts at $15 per employee per month for large companies and $23 per employee per month for small teams with fewer than 49 employees.
paragraph2: Ask Proxy works over SMS. You can text “start” to 820-732-2625. Caddy Image Credits:Caddy Caddy is an AI assistant that turns the information scattered across your phone into things you can actually act on. It lives in iMessage for iPhone users and RCS for Android users, so there’s no separate app or inbox to constantly check. For instance, an email contains an appointment that needs to be added to your calendar or a friend sends a list of things to pick up. Instead of worrying about all the details getting buried, Caddy connects to your calendars and conversations, then identifies things that may require action. It can add events to your calendar, set reminders, keep track of follow-ups, and even do research for you. Caddy has been available in public beta since April 2026. Comma Image Credits:Comma Comma is designed to manage tasks across both work and everyday life. Comma carries tasks through to completion, checking its own work and determining when a task is finished. Completed work is surfaced for review when a decision or approval is needed. It also proactively notifies users and recommends the next steps. It can work across a user’s browser, computer, and files, while remaining accessible remotely through messaging apps such as Signal, Telegram, and WeChat. Comma maintains context and memory across devices and conversations, and can deliver daily briefings, flag urgent matters, and summarize recorded calls.
paragraph3: Comma is free to start and open source. Fambot Image Credits:Fambot Fambot is an AI-powered “chief of staff” for families, designed to bring together the many moving parts of family life, including school communications, sports activities, meal planning, calendars, and other day-to-day responsibilities, and turn them into an organized plan. The service is designed to work across both an app and text messages. Fambot is available on iOS devices, Android devices, and the web, and families can also interact with it directly over SMS. Every night, Fambot automatically sends a summary of the following day, including upcoming events, to-dos, and details such as school uniform or packing requirements. Parents can reply to those messages to ask questions, check information, or make changes to their calendar. Fambot currently connects to Gmail, Google Calendar, Outlook, and WhatsApp, with support for Apple Calendar planned for the future. The company launched in beta in early September 2026 and has raised $3.5 million in pre-seed funding. The service is currently free during the beta period, but Fambot expects to eventually charge roughly the equivalent of a Netflix subscription. Folk Image Credits:Folk Folk is designed to be an AI assistant you can reach through iMessage, WhatsApp, and Telegram. It can remember personal context, manage reminders, research topics, track flights, handle email, and perform real-world tasks such as restaurant reservations. One distinction is that Folk runs on its own private cloud computer. It can also run code and execute multi-step tasks rather than merely responding conversationally.
paragraph4: Folk launched its beta in May 2026, and it’s available for free but also offers a Pro subscription for $8.33/month if you want unlimited tasks running in the background. Instinct Image Credits:Instinct Instinct first made headlines after raising $350 million at a $2.5 billion valuation. In September 2026, it raised $1 billion, valuing it at $10 billion. The always-available agent can take actions on your behalf, rather than simply answer questions. Users can communicate with Instinct by text or voice and connect it to the apps and services they already use, such as email, calendar, Google Workspace, and more. The company says early users have used Instinct for tasks ranging from planning trips and buying groceries to booking tickets and canceling subscriptions. In September, Instinct began giving users dedicated email addresses for their assistants. The idea is to let Instinct create and manage accounts on a user’s behalf without filling the user’s personal inbox. The agent can use its address to sign up for services, contact businesses, follow up on requests, and handle tasks that require an email account. (However, this level of autonomy has also raised concerns about privacy and security.) It’s also begun rolling out support for placing calls. The company remains in private beta.
paragraph5: Iris Image Credits:Iris Powered by Hermes Agent, Iris is designed to let users delegate tasks to an AI assistant directly through iMessage. Users can connect the apps they use and hand over a task with a simple message. The agent then works through the required steps, while retaining relevant context from previous interactions. It’s also designed to follow up with users proactively rather than waiting for another request. title: I hope Apple’s touchscreen MacBook takes some lessons from this Lenovo laptop
title_bn: আশা করি অ্যাপলের টাচস্ক্রিন ম্যাকবুক এই লেনোভো ল্যাপটপ থেকে কিছু শিক্ষা নিয়েছে।
author: TechPulse
excerpt: It looks like the long-rumored touchscreen MacBook might actually get announced next week, and after using the Lenovo Yoga 9n for our testing of Nvidia's RTX Spark platform, it got me thinking: this is a lot of what I want from a touchscreen MacBook.
paragraph1: It looks like the long-rumored touchscreen MacBook might actually get announced next week, and after using the Lenovo Yoga 9n for our testing of Nvidia’s RTX Spark platform, it got me thinking: this is a lot of what I want from a touchscreen MacBook.Like the Apple silicon in modern MacBook Pros, RTX Spark is an Arm-based processor with a beefy integrated GPU and lots of unified memory. And the Yoga is the most fun RTX Spark laptop so far because it’s a 16-inch 2-in-1 convertible with a stylus. Its Nvidia-powered compatriots also have touchscreens, like most Windows laptops, but they’re conventional clamshell designs.The Lenovo Yoga does all your typical 2-in-1 stuff: it can be used as a clamshell laptop, and it can fold its hinge all the way back for tent mode and tablet modes. As a tablet, you can use it in either landscape or portrait orientation, and getting the keyboard out of the way is great for watching movies, playing games with a controller, or integrating your laptop into a multi-monitor desk setup with keyboard and mouse.2-in-1s can be seen as a weird compromise between laptops and tablets.
paragraph2: I just think they’re neat.The Yoga 9n’s included stylus works for note-taking and drawing on its excellent OLED display, but you can also use it on the haptic trackpad for a Wacom-like experience, without blocking the screen with your hand. And the stylus is magnetic, allowing it to attach to the Yoga’s lid — either on its own, or while housed in its case. I particularly enjoy using the Yoga’s stylus for photo retouching in Lightroom Classic or Photoshop. I haven’t used a stylus for that kind of work in ages, since I gave up my old Wacom, but having one that works on either the screen or the trackpad is incredibly convenientI expect a touchscreen MacBook Pro would have Apple Pencil support. And like on the Lenovo, it would go a long way to get me back to using a stylus for retouching. But I hope that also like the Lenovo, it works on the trackpad too — the more options, the better.
paragraph3: And if a touch-enabled MacBook supports the Apple Pencil (which it should), I’m also hoping it attaches to the laptop, both for convenience and for wireless charging, as on the iPad Pro. Lenovo’s stylus relies on USB-C charging, which is fine, but not as convenient as always having it charged and ready to go while attached to your laptop.1/2The Yoga 9n’s stylus works on both the trackpad and the screen.I don’t expect Apple to make a standard convertible laptop after all this time. Simply joining Windows manufacturers in making a 2-in-1 or swapping the MacBook Pro’s Mini LED for a touchscreen OLED and calling it a day doesn’t seem very Apple. I’m hoping for something special, like Apple’s own take on the Microsoft Surface Laptop Studio — a clever idea that brought the touchscreen forward instead of flipping it backwards — or something totally fresh. And there are hints in macOS 27 that Apple is updating to Golden Gate to make touch functions feel more natural than just poking and prodding at things designed for a mouse cursor.
paragraph4: As fun as I find 2-in-1 Windows laptops and Chromebooks, using those desktop operating systems with a finger or a stylus can get clunky.My hopes are high for Apple to wow us, because this MacBook Pro with touch is sure to be expensive. And Apple’s recent design decisions aren’t faultless. The HomeView’s lack of apps is perplexing. The iPhone Duo is a little messy. Current MacBooks are so great, it’s easy to forget the butterfly keyboard fiasco wasn’t all that long ago. After all this time of holding out on adding a touchscreen to the MacBook, Apple has to make it worth it.
paragraph5: Photography by Antonio G. Di Benedetto / The VergeFollow topics and authors from this story to see more like this in your personalized homepage feed and to receive email updates.Antonio G.

title: Proton hosts Flock map revealing over 300,000 cameras, defying cease-and-desist threats against creator
title_bn: প্রোটন ৩০০,০০০ ক্যামেরার উপর ফ্লক ম্যাপ প্রকাশ করেছে, যা স্রষ্টার বিরুদ্ধে থামার হুমকিকে প্রত্যাখ্যান করে
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Privacy-focused firm Proton AG just decided to host the Flock camera map that a security researcher published last month.
paragraph1: Proton AG, which provides privacy-focused services like Proton Mail and Proton VPN, has decided to host the Flock camera map that security researcher Joshua Michael built from leaked Flock data. While the original Flock Surveillance Map is still available online, its creator is facing legal threats from the company, especially after Flock sent the researcher a cease-and-desist letter.
paragraph2: In addition, Michael’s website is accessible only from within the U.S.
paragraph3: , requiring users outside the country to use a VPN to access it.By contrast, Proton’s Flock camera map is easily accessible worldwide.
paragraph4: Its location in Switzerland also makes it a little more complicated for the surveillance company to take legal action. Its move to preserve Michael’s work also follows the company’s privacy ethos.
paragraph5: Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.

title: Top Stories: Apple 'Pro and Tell' Debut, iPhone Duo Launch, and More
title_bn: শীর্ষ সংবাদঃ অ্যাপলের 'প্রো অ্যান্ড টেল' ডিবেট, আইফোন ডুও লঞ্চ, এবং আরও অনেক কিছু
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Yet another busy week for Apple saw a teaser for even more product announcements coming next week, plus we got the highly anticipated launch of Apple's first foldable smartphone, the iPhone Duo. Other news this week included Verizon announcing a heft
paragraph1: Yet another busy week for Apple saw a teaser for even more product announcements coming next week, plus we got the highly anticipated launch of Apple's first foldable smartphone, the iPhone Duo. Other news this week included Verizon announcing a hefty monthly charge for the iPhone Handoff feature that lets two iPhones share the same phone number, while the public release of iOS 27.2 and related updates appears to be right around the corner, so read on below for all of the details on these stories and more! Top Stories Apple Announcing New Products Next Week: 'Pro and Tell' The Apple launch parade continues, with Apple teasing another set of product introductions next week under the tagline "Pro and tell." Apple is holding a media "experience" for the new products in Los Angeles on Wednesday, October 28, so we're expecting a wave of press releases that day. The event tagline and animated logo are suggestive of the long-rumored touchscreen MacBook that looks like it will be appearing as part of the MacBook Pro family rather than as a separate "MacBook Ultra." We're also expecting an iPad mini 8 with an OLED display, as well as updated iMac and low-end 14-inch MacBook Pro models featuring the M6 chip. Be sure to check out our overview of launch expectations for more details.
paragraph2: iPhone Duo Brings Back Long Lines at Apple Stores After Apple saw "extraordinary" demand for the iPhone Duo on pre-order launch day last week that quickly saw shipping estimates slip all the way until January 2027, some customers held out hope of being able to score a unit on a walk-in basis at an Apple Store when sales began on Friday. The situation marked a return to long lines at many Apple retail stores, a phenomenon that had largely disappeared in recent years as Apple emphasized offering online orders with pickup appointments rather than first come, first served walk-in sales. Some retail store staff were advised to discourage walk-in customers from coming in on Friday with expectations of buying the device, and Apple said it would have "limited" availability of iPhone Duo in its stores in most countries. A few lucky customers were able to score walk-in purchases of the iPhone Duo, and Apple appears to be reviving online ordering for in-store pickup that was quickly removed under the crush of pre-order day. Here's What Apple's Apps Look Like on the iPhone Duo We had been a bit light on details about just what apps would look like on the iPhone Duo's new form factor, but App Store screenshots revealed ahead of the launch how some more of Apple's stock apps have been adapted for the new device. Early media reviews also gave us a bit better look at the situation, with many noting that third-party apps may not look great until developers get them updated, as by default they continue to show in a traditional iPhone aspect ratio and layout surrounded by black bars. Verizon Will Charge $10 a Month for iPhone Handoff With iOS 27, Apple introduced a new feature called iPhone Handoff that lets you quickly swap back-and-forth between two phones with one phone number. The feature seems particularly convenient for the iPhone Duo launch, with some users perhaps wanting to carry different iPhone form factors at different times depending on their needs.
paragraph3: iPhone Handoff does require carrier support, which is still quite limited, and carriers can charge extra for those looking to take advantage of the feature. T-Mobile was the first U.S. carrier to add support for it with pricing set at $5 per month, and Verizon has now announced that it too will be adding iPhone Handoff support but at a heftier $10-per-month price point. Apple Releases iOS 27.2 Release Candidate Apple this week seeded the release candidates of iOS 27.2 and related updates for testing purposes, suggesting a full public release could come next week. The beta period was used to test a revamped Health app, but that has been removed for the public release as Apple will continue testing it before rolling it out to everyone later this year.
paragraph4: Other feature additions include a new icon and theme for Apple Music alongside a just-announced rebrand, user profiles in the Apple TV app, and an expansion of Siri AI support to new languages. Apple Planning 'HomeView Max' With 9-Inch, 360-Degree Screen Apple's new HomeView smart home hub hasn't made it into customers' hands yet, but we're hearing continued rumors about a more advanced version that could arrive in the next year or two. According to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, this "HomeView Max" will include a 9-inch display (up from 7 inches in the standard HomeView) and include a robotic arm that will allow the display to swivel a full 360º to maintain visibility of the screen and keep subjects in view during video calls as they move around a room. title: Laika has spent 20 years building up to Wildwood
title_bn: লাইকা ২০ বছর ধরে ওয়াইল্ডউড তৈরি করছে
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Across several decades in Hollywood, Caleb Deschanel has seen a lot. He served as cinematographer on films like The Passion of the Christ and The Patriot, worked on sequences in The Godfather and Titanic, and directed a few episodes of Twin Peaks. Ev
paragraph1: Across several decades in Hollywood, Caleb Deschanel has seen a lot. He served as cinematographer on films like The Passion of the Christ and The Patriot, worked on sequences in The Godfather and Titanic, and directed a few episodes of Twin Peaks. Even still, nothing could quite prepare him for his first stop-motion project: working as the cinematographer on Wildwood, the latest release from Coraline studio Laika. While he knew that stop-motion was a long and involved process, he was still surprised by just how much work went into these movies. “When I started I thought it was one thing, and then I quickly found out that it was another thing,” Deschanel says. “It was much more complicated than I expected.”Wildwood has been a long time coming. Laika CEO Travis Knight originally optioned the rights for the book of the same name, written by Decemberists frontman Colin Meloy, in 2011. But production didn’t begin until a decade later. “I’ve been working on it in some form or another for 16 years,” Knight, who also directed Wildwood, says.
paragraph2: “The reason why I stuck with it, the reason why I had to make this movie no matter what, is because of what it meant to me personally. Underneath it all, it’s a story about love and loss and grief, it’s about the impossible things that love asks of us, and that meant something to me personally in a very profound way.”It’s also the biggest production Laika has ever undertaken. Wildwood tells the story of a young girl named Prue who has to venture into the “impassable wilderness” that surrounds Portland in order to find her baby brother. When she enters the forest she discovers a fantasy realm reminiscent of Narnia, with magical spells, talking animals, and warring factions. It required nearly 50 animators and more than 200 puppets to pull it off, and the film is full of ambitious sequences, like a 12-minute battle with dozens of soldiers and a chase scene through a bustling Portland, where Prue’s brother is carried away by a gigantic murder of crows.Image: LaikaImage: LaikaAccording to head of animation Brad Schiff, the studio’s ethos involves mixing “old-school craft with modern technology.” With each project, he says, Laika develops new techniques. If something works well, they then push the idea even further on the next project. For instance, on Laika’s previous film, Missing Link, the main character was outfitted with a diaphragm so that when an animator turned a screw on the puppet’s back, the diaphragm could expand or contract, creating the illusion that it was breathing.
paragraph3: This has since become the standard for puppets in Laika’s films.These may sound like small details, but over the years they add up. For costume designer Deb Cook, there wasn’t a single innovation on Wildwood that stood out to her, but rather the sheer number of tools she had at her disposal. “Over time we’ve gathered together a library of techniques that we’ve been able to put into practice on this movie,” she says. This was especially important on Wildwood, which features a huge range of costumes; in the city sequences everyone is dressed in modern clothing, whereas in the forest characters have more fantastical looks.“It was much more complicated than I expected.”For Wildwood, many of the advancements came down to materials. The costumes made use of more flexible fabrics, for example, and the team also engineered a new process for creating silicone that’s lighter and more durable than what they previously used. “We’ve done this so we can wean ourselves off of foam latex, which is stinky and it shrinks over time, and five years later it kind of just crumbles,” says Oliver Jones, head of characters and practical effects. “There are advantages to rethinking a lot of these materials that were our go-to probably since King Kong.
paragraph4: ”The scale of Wildwood has also forced the studio to adopt another seemingly much more boring practice: being better organized. “They’ve been misplaced,” Cook says, when asked if she’s ever lost a puppet. “There’s now a very sophisticated tracking system because there are so many moving parts, and so many stages around the studio.”And while much has been said about the large and elaborate sequences in the film — Knight says the epic battle scene is “probably the most technically challenging thing that we’ve ever done” — all of these techniques are designed to imbue more humanity into characters that are portrayed by puppets. In that regard, small details like the flow of fabric or the impression of breathing are vitally important.Image: LaikaImage: Laika“We also have really subtle and intimate scenes, quiet scenes that don’t have a lot of flash, that have virtually no sound design or music, where the only thing that you’re experiencing is the grief of a father talking about a secret that he’s been holding on to for 15 years, or a quiet moment of a woman grieving the loss of her son,” Knight explains. “These are moments where you have nowhere to hide and the performances of these little puppets — these little assemblages of steel and silicon and fabric that have no life of their own — completely spring to life because of the hand and the artistry of the human behind it. Those are the moments that I’m most proud of.”In this way, the long road to Wildwood hitting theaters makes a lot of sense. Laika has been around for just over 20 years, and over the course of each film the studio has innovated to steadily push its craft forward.
paragraph5: Knight may have been thinking about the film for 16 years, but creating the version that is coming out in 2026 wouldn’t have been possible without all of the learnings spread across films like ParaNorman and Kubo and the Two Strings.For Knight, it’s been especially gratifying to bring it to life with a team of both Laika veterans and newcomers, including not only Deschanel but also a handful of young animators for whom Wildwood was their first feature film project. Some were young enough that Coraline, Laika’s very first film, was what inspired them to get into the field in the first place. “I was really moved by that,” says Knight. “It also made me feel old as shit.”Wildwood is in theaters now.Follow topics and authors from this story to see more like this in your personalized homepage feed and to receive email updates.

title: It’s time to find a new browser
title_bn: এখন নতুন ব্রাউজার খুজার সময়
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Hi, friends! Welcome to Installer No. 149, your guide to the best and Verge-iest stuff in the world. (If you're new here, welcome, happy It Actually Feels Like Fall Now At Least In My Neighborhood), and also you can read all the old editions at the I
paragraph1: Hi, friends! Welcome to Installer No. 149, your guide to the best and Verge-iest stuff in the world. (If you’re new here, welcome, happy It Actually Feels Like Fall Now At Least In My Neighborhood), and also you can read all the old editions at the Installer homepage.)This week, I’ve been reading about Demis Hassabis and computer chips and permafrost, enjoying the first episodes of Machine Gods,filming the next season of Version History (pet season!), seeing You Can See Everythingand then reading and listening to absolutely everything about it, painstakingly updating all the stuff in my 1Password, making tiny documents with Tiny Little Office, watching Conan O’Brien own Subway Takesthe way he once owned Hot Ones,finally getting properly good at CapCut, and blasting the soundtrack to The Mandalorian and Grogu all workday long.I also have for you a new AI assistant, the most Duo-y new app for the iPhone Duo, my hunt for the next great browser, and much more. Let’s do this.(As always, the best part of Installer is your ideas and tips. What are you playing / reading / watching / listening to / modding with Claude this week? Tell me everything: installer@theverge.com. And if you know someone else who might enjoy Installer, forward it to them and tell them to subscribe here.)The DropCall of Duty: Modern Warfare 4. Obviously, Grand Theft Auto VI is the biggest game release of the year, but a new COD is always a big deal. This one doesn’t sound like some grand reinvention of the form, but rather an even more playable, even more powerful version of what works. I was particularly excited to hear that the campaign mode is a huge improvement this time.The Blink Mini 4K. Ring cameras get a lot more shine, but Amazon’s cheaper brand also makes some pretty good stuff. This one’s part of a whole new lineup of devices, but $80 for a 4K camera with two-way audio and plenty of smart security features? Not a bad deal.
paragraph2: JustWatch TV. As streaming services get incessantly more expensive, I’m starting to bail on some paid services and spend more time on the free ones. JustWatch’s new service is surprisingly well-stocked out of the gate — I suspect they’ve been watching what people search for, and making some smart content bets.Claude Duet. Here’s Anthropic’s answer to Muse, Instinct, and Dots. Duet seems to be focused on helping you get stuff done at work by making to-do lists, coordinating meetings, and compiling data for you. Still waitlist-only right now, but it’ll be interesting to see if it’s as thirsty for attention as Muse is.Wildwood. Before you see this gorgeous, by all accounts excellent stop-motion movie, read everything you can about how it was made. Not a pixel of generative AI in sight, just an unbelievable amount of hard work and human creativity. Humans rock, artists rock, this movie rocks.The Teenage Engineering EP-35. When you go to buy this thing, it’s technically called “Life is fantastic!” Which, sure. This thing is a battery powered, multi-input, multi-instrument amp with lots of effects. As always, it is extremely cool-looking. I have no use for it, and I want it quite badly.Nintendo Switch Sports Resort. Nintendo basically hasn’t changed the formula here since Wii Sports from two decades ago, and I have absolutely no problem with that. Anything that gives me that super-active tennis and bowling (plus volleyball, boxing, thumb wrestling, and more) is a win in my book.Delta 2.
paragraph3: 0. The next couple of weeks are going to be full of interesting app updates as developers try to figure out what to make of Apple’s foldable phone. But one of the best is already available; Delta can now pretty successfully cosplay as any handheld console ever. (Plus the Sega Genesis!)Kindle Plus. This is mostly just a rebranding of Kindle Unlimited, but Amazon put a couple of interesting new features in its $12 monthly reading subscription, including AI-narrated audiobooks. I am dubious of those, but excited about expanding access to audiobooks. We’ll see.SpotlightThe worst news of the week here in the Installerverse is that Arc is going away. This was obviously coming: The Browser Company bailed on Arc two years ago in favor of the more AI-centric Dia, and Arc has been in maintenance mode ever since. But now it’s not just being ignored, it’s going away. By Christmas, you won’t even be able to use the app anymore.So now a lot of us are stuck looking for another browser. There are a million new ones out there, many of them somewhere between “heavily inspired by Arc” and “a direct copy of Arc I made in Codex this morning.” I need to test a lot of them. I don’t know exactly where I’ll land yet, but I figured I’d share a bunch of the ones I’m looking at:Dia. It has recently gotten a lot of Arc’s best features, and some of the AI stuff is pretty cool. (And mercifully easy to turn off.) The Browser Company’s attention to aesthetic detail remains the best in the biz, so I’m starting here.Zen. A total ripoff of Arc, and I mean that as a compliment.
paragraph4: Zen runs on Mozilla’s Gecko engine rather than Chromium, which is a win for anyone looking for a little less Google influence in their lives. Last time I tried Zen it was a little buggy and unpolished, but I’ve heard it’s come a long way.Orion. I am a dedicated and very happy Kagi user, and I’ve heard good things about how simple and resource-friendly the company’s browser is. Given the seamless Kagi integration, I sort of hope this one wins for me.Vivaldi. I used Vivaldi for a while, and I love how customizable it is. I eventually got it set up exactly the way I wanted it. But right next to all that customization is just a feeling of fiddliness, and I couldn’t quite get comfortable in the browser. Might try again.Helium. The opposite of Vivaldi, this is a super minimalist, no-frills browser. It’s probably what I need, honestly.Firefox. Its confusing stance on AI aside, I like a lot of the recent design and feature choices Firefox has made. I’m also intrigued by some of the Firefox forks, like Waterfox and Floorp, which give it even more customization options.Brave. Brave has always felt too heavy to me, and like it’s always trying to convince me to use more of its own proprietary (and often underpowered) features. But it seems to always win in privacy comparisons, so I might need to give it a go again.On mobile, it’s easy. Quiche is my favorite iOS browser by a mile.
paragraph5: Arc was never great on Android, so I’m betting most of us never switched there in the first place.There are also the default browsers, of course, like Chrome, Safari, and Edge. But each of those browsers continues to fail me in one way or another, and so my search continues. If you’ve found your browser of the future, tell me all about it! Otherwise, I’ll report back here periodically through my journey.CrowdsourcedHere’s what the Installer community is into this week. I want to know what you’re into right now as well! Email installer@theverge.com or message me on Signal — @davidpierce.11 — with your recommendations for anything and everything, and we’ll feature some of our favorites here every week. For even more great recommendations, check out the replies to this post on Threads and this post on Bluesky.“Youth is an absolute SCREAM on HBO Max at the moment.” — Jonathan“Todoist has a stellar integration with Siri AI that has finally made me fully commit to just using it If you delete Reminders, Todoist becomes the default on Siri AI and you can add a to-do to any project with tag AND location support (using Apple Maps saved locations like home and work!) title: A 1,000-mile cloud on Mars may reveal physics never seen in nature
title_bn: মঙ্গলে ১,০০০ মাইলের একটি মেঘ প্রকৃতিতে দেখা যায় না এমন পদার্থবিজ্ঞান প্রকাশ করতে পারে
author: TechPulse
excerpt: A new model suggests Mars may host ice-forming physics never directly observed before.
paragraph1: On Earth, clouds usually form when water vapor creates droplets or ice crystals in the presence of tiny particles, such as dust or salt. The new study, published in Nature Geoscience, instead suggests AMEC could be forming through so-called homogeneous nucleation, where vapor changes directly into ice crystals on its own without any help from debris. “It’s akin to droplets of condensation appearing in the middle of a room, rather than on a window,” Hernández-Bernal explained.
paragraph2: “It’s wholly unexpected.” This phenomenon requires extreme conditions—a sharp temperature drop of 30° Celsius within 10 minutes and high relative humidity. The Arsia Mons volcano also plays a key role.
paragraph3: When wind current hits the 65,000-foot-tall volcano, it creates a powerful wave that launches moist air high in the atmosphere in a matter of minutes. Scientists have assumed a similar phenomenon could occur in the upper atmospheres of other planets, including Venus and even Earth, but it has never been observed. That’s not too surprising given the extreme air humidity required for this phenomenon, which is more than 100,000 times greater than any value measured on Earth.
paragraph4: Before this modeling, it was not known that these humidity levels existed on Mars either. “We don’t have nearly as much information about Mars’ atmosphere as we do about Earth’s, so reproducing the AMEC to this degree is a big success,” said Hernández-Bernal, adding, “the result is remarkable.” This story originally appeared on WIRED Czech Republic and Slovakia and has been translated from Czech.

title: Texas has suspended 17 data center construction permits and shut down automated portal that rubber-stamped projects
title_bn: টেক্সাস ১৭টি ডেটা সেন্টারের নির্মাণের অনুমতি স্থগিত করেছে এবং স্বয়ংক্রিয় পোর্টাল বন্ধ করেছে যা রাবার-স্ট্যাম্পযুক্ত প্রকল্পগুলিকে বন্ধ করে দিয়েছে
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Texas has suspended 17 data center construction permits and shut down the automated portal used to approve them
paragraph1: Texas has suspended the construction permits of 17 data center projects and disabled a web portal that automated filing for new permits after it was discovered that they were still being issued a month after calls for the process to be paused.
paragraph2: Governor Greg Abbott asked for new permits to be halted in September 2026, but watchdog groups FracTracker Alliance and Public Citizen both published reports detailing more than two dozen permits issued to Texas data center projects, reports 404 Media.
paragraph3: Now, the portal that previously automatically authorized permits is unavailable.
paragraph4: “TCEQ’s electronic filing application used for automatic authorizations has been temporarily shut down to ensure all applications are reviewed by agency staff to determine if they are related to data centers," a message on the website reads.
paragraph5: Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
bangla_paragraph1: টেক্সাস ১৭টি ডেটা সেন্টার প্রকল্পের নির্মাণের অনুমতি স্থগিত করেছে এবং একটি ওয়েব পোর্টালকে অক্ষম করেছে যা নতুন অনুমতির জন্য ফাইলিংকে স্বয়ংক্রিয় করেছে।
bangla_paragraph2: গভর্নর গ্রেগ অ্যাবট ২০২৬ সালের সেপ্টেম্বরে নতুন অনুমতি বন্ধ করার জন্য অনুরোধ করেছিলেন, কিন্তু ফ্রেকট্র্যাকার অ্যালায়েন্স এবং পাবলিক সিটিজেন উভয়ই টেক্সাসের ডেটা সেন্টার প্রকল্পগুলিতে জারি করা দুই ডজনেরও বেশি অনুমতির বিশদ বিবরণ প্রকাশ করেছে, 404 মিডিয়া রিপোর্ট করেছে।

title: I dumped 8 popular Android apps for these better open-source alternatives
title_bn: আমি এই উন্মুক্ত-সোর্স বিকল্পগুলির জন্য ৮টি জনপ্রিয় অ্যান্ড্রয়েড অ্যাপ ফেলে দিয়েছি
author: TechPulse
excerpt: There’s some great open-source apps for managing passwords, playing podcasts, and more.
paragraph1: Andy Walker / Android AuthorityAdd Android Authority on Google: I’ve been on a mission to replace as many Android apps on my phone with open-source alternatives as feasible. Last month, I detailed my preferred replacements for Google’s more popular apps. Today, I’m looking to address some of the more important stragglers on my phone that weren’t made in Mountain View.Not every app on my phone is made by Google, but that doesn’t mean there aren’t good open-source alternatives for these products. In fact, while some of Google’s apps are rather difficult to replace due to their unmatched service integration, many of the apps on the list below are far simpler to switch out.Which Google app would you find most difficult to replace on your phone?1066 votesLastPass to BitwardenAndy Walker / Android AuthorityLet’s start with the most important app on my phone, my password manager. Instead of remembering every single individual password to multiple accounts, password managers require just one password to unlock the vault. It forms the heart of my online security strategy while reducing my reliance on my forgetful mind.I previously used LastPass for this task. Its strengths included its ubiquity — I could install it on practically any device, access it through almost every browser, or view my passwords on the web if need be. However, it has faced various security challenges in recent years and is now desktop- or mobile-only, rather than both. That lack of flexibility is a big problem.Several years ago, I took all these gripes into account and decided to switch to Bitwarden. It took me a while to make the swap, but Bitwarden has been a stellar, if not more accomplished, alternative.
paragraph2: It offers all the perks of LastPass, including the option to self-host passwords, an excellent security track record, and cross-device syncing. I use it daily, and I’ve yet to run into a game-breaking issue.Reddit to RedReaderAndy Walker / Android AuthorityI won’t beat around the bush here, either: the Reddit app is horrible. In fact, I’ve never used the platform’s official app for my thread browsing needs. Apps like RIF, Infinity, and Boost made my Reddit experience so much better, but when the company cut off API access to most of them several years ago, I needed an alternative.Enter RedReader. This open-source Reddit app is exempt from the API restrictions that affect other apps because it provides accessibility features that Reddit doesn’t offer. This means I get the full benefits of many of the third-party apps I mentioned above in 2026.This includes ad and sponsored content blocking, a far less cluttered interface with plenty of customization possibilities, versatile content playback options, and accessibility options that’ll benefit everyone. These include more obvious comment indents and individually focusable lines in posts.Adobe Reader to PaperKnife+Andy Walker / Android AuthorityAdobe Reader is a hugely powerful PDF app that can manipulate the format in various ways. Many assume it’s the only app that can handle tasks like signing and merging documents, but that couldn’t be further from the truth. There’s an open-source app that does all this and more.I’ve been using PaperKnife+ for several months now and haven’t looked back. It can attach signatures, lock or unlock documents, compress them, extract pages or text, and convert PDFs to other formats.
paragraph3: As its name hints at, it’s a pocketknife for all the various PDF tasks you could ever come across.The UI is wonderfully simple and clutter-free, too, and packs so much utility into a free package.ChatGPT to AI HubAndy Walker / Android AuthorityThe ChatGPT app was once a fixture on my Android phone. It’s my preferred general AI taskmaster thanks to its quick responses and solid output. But using a standalone app dedicated to one AI chatbot does have its limitations, the obvious one being a lack of flexibility. If I doubt ChatGPT’s output or want a second opinion, I’d need to ensure that I have Claude or DeepSeek installed as well. That’s just not practical.AI Hub solves this problem more than a hundred times over. There aren’t many of my accounts without this double security layer.My previous 2FA service, Authy, served me well for years, but recent moves and shake-ups haven’t instilled much confidence. I disliked its shift from a universal service to one primarily accessed on my phone.
paragraph4: Then there are the various security lapses it has faced in its history.After dragging my feet for years, I recently switched to Ente Auth. This open-source platform is highly extensible and can be run as a self-hosted vault or a cloud-hosted one, giving me control over how I access my code. If using the latter setup, these can be retrieved in myriad ways, from its mobile platform to browser extensions. Lastly, Ente Auth‘s Android app is far more accommodating, packs sensible usability upgrades like highlighting future codes, and plenty of categorization options.Raindrop to LinkoraAndy Walker / Android AuthorityThis was one of the more difficult switches I’ve made on my phone. Since a bookmarking or read-it-later app has become one of the centerpieces of my productivity flow, changing it could knock down several other dominoes.My service of choice was Raindrop. It provides easy multi-device sync smarts, which allows me to save links on my PC and read them on my phone, packs various organizational smarts, and a pleasant web and app UI. It isn’t quite Pocket, but it does an admirable job at replacing it.I recently switched to Linkora, an open-source Android bookmarking app that lets me self-host my saves. That alone gives me loads of flexibility, but it also means it doesn’t have the ease of use of Raindrop. That said, this hasn’t been as big of a problem as I first thought. Since I use Link to Windows, which allows me to open Android apps on my Windows desktop, I don’t necessarily need desktop access to save links.Either way, Linkora offers more comprehensive organization options, including multiple and nested folders, archiving older links, and the ability to save web pages for offline viewing.
paragraph5: Podcast Republic to PodiumAndy Walker / Android AuthorityPodcast Republic is a comprehensive Android podcasting app. Overflowing with features, it can often feel overwhelming to new and experienced users alike. But since I find it difficult to focus on primary tasks, I often find myself tweaking settings instead of doing the one thing the app is made for: listening to podcasts.There are plenty of open-source podcasting apps on Android, but one of my newer finds is called Podium. It adopts Google’s Material 3 Expressive stylings to ensure it looks right at home on modern Android phones. It packs podcast discovery features, download options for offline listening, and sync smarts for podcast cloud platforms like Gpodder.Obsidian to JoplinAndy Walker / Android AuthorityObsidian has the same problem as Podcast Republic — it’s tremendously powerful and extendible, but again, this counts against it for some users. For me, Obsidian was my primary writing app for many years, facilitating my various ideation and editing tasks. title: PHP2Shell: Who Is At Risk And How Can Businesses Stay Safe?
title_bn: PHP2Shell: ঝুঁকিতে কারা এবং কিভাবে ব্যবসা নিরাপদ থাকতে পারে?
author: TechPulse
excerpt: PHP, a programming language used to build websites, is at the centre of a major security concern after researchers uncovered…
paragraph1: SUMMARYTwo critical flaws in PHP could allow hackers to run malicious code on vulnerable servers without logging in. Websites, online businesses and enterprise applications could face data theft, service disruption and unauthorised access. Rated 9.2 out of 10 for severity, the vulnerabilities were patched on October 21, 2026, but businesses must still check for exposure and possible attacks. PHP, a programming language used to build websites, is at the centre of a major security concern after researchers uncovered two critical flaws that could let hackers take control of vulnerable servers. Called PHP2Shell, the vulnerabilities could let attackers run malicious code on affected systems without needing to log in. Since the vulnerabilities lie in PHP itself rather than individual websites built on it, businesses cannot rely on website-level security measures alone to stay protected. The vulnerabilities affect specific PHP versions, and fixes were released on October 21, 2026. Businesses must now check whether they are running affected versions, install the updates and investigate whether hackers exploited the flaws before the fixes were applied. The discovery story involves both independent research and AI-assisted security work. Security firm Calif credited pseudonymous researcher LCFR with first discovering PHP2Shell and developing a working exploit. Separately, AI company OpenAI said security research firm Calif identified a critical flaw using its GPT-5.6 Sol model, while cybersecurity firm Wiz independently discovered and reported both vulnerabilities. OpenAI’s disclosure describes the collaboration that helped prepare fixes before public disclosure.
paragraph2: The episode also highlights a growing cybersecurity concern: AI tools are helping researchers uncover complex security flaws, but organisations must be equally agile to fix them. Which Businesses Face The Risk? PHP powers around 70% of websites globally. This highlights the language’s reach, but does not mean that 70% of websites are vulnerable. The actual risk depends on the PHP version, server configuration and exposure to attack. The vulnerabilities can allow attackers to run code remotely on affected servers without authentication. Amruta Moktali, chief product officer at Skyflow, a data privacy and security platform, said initial industry reports cited millions of potentially exposed instances because PHP is widely used across websites, content management systems, hosting environments and enterprise applications. For Indian businesses, Moktali said the immediate priority should be internet-facing PHP systems that handle sensitive information. These include systems connected to payment services, customer databases and identity and authentication tools. Small businesses and website operators may face additional challenges if they depend on third-party hosting providers or lack dedicated security teams. They may not know which PHP version their websites use or whether their provider has installed the relevant updates. Sooraj Sathyanarayanan, a cybersecurity researcher and program manager at privacy-focused web browser Brave, said successful exploitation could allow attackers to execute code without logging in or requiring user interaction. Depending on the server’s permissions, this could expose customer data and credentials, enable website changes or allow malware to be installed. However, the level of risk depends on the PHP build and server configuration, so not all installations are equally vulnerable.
paragraph3: Legacy systems are another concern, as the flaw occurs within PHP’s core engine before an application’s own code runs. “One thing organisations must keep in mind with PHP2Shell is that because this flaw triggers inside the core PHP engine before any application code executes, traditional application-level safeguards won’t stop it,” said Niv Lanyado, security research team lead for PHP at JFrog, a software supply chain security company. RECOMMENDED FOR yOU He stressed that organisations need visibility into all their systems, particularly older PHP installations that may no longer receive security updates, so they can be patched or isolated. Fixing The Software Is Not Enough The PHP team released fixed versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 on October 21. Its official security advisory says there are no complete mitigations and urges users to update. Organisations should first identify where PHP is running across their servers, cloud environments and third-party hosting arrangements.
paragraph4: They should then check which installations are affected and confirm that the updated software is active. According to Aditya Narayana K, the cofounder of cybersecurity company focused on AI security, Mirror Security, organisations need a repeatable process to identify vulnerabilities, fix them and verify that the fixes work. He pointed to the NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 as a useful guide for managing this process. “Organisations must confirm that patches are active and the vulnerability is no longer reproducible, rather than assuming that applying a patch resolves the risk,” Narayana said. Where immediate patching is not possible, businesses should follow official guidance from PHP and their hosting or software providers. Temporary measures may reduce exposure, but they are not a substitute for a complete fix. Unsupported installations may need to be upgraded or isolated until they can be secured. The incident has also raised questions about whether businesses can keep pace with AI-assisted vulnerability discovery. Sriram Krishnan, a technology investor and former general partner at venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), wrote on X that the PHP disclosure will make the ecosystem safer by finding long-lurking issues. “However, the entire software supply chain will need the muscles to rapidly build and deploy fixes. We might need a lot more public + private partnerships to secure infrastructure across the country.” How Can Businesses Check For A Breach? Patching closes a known vulnerability, but it does not establish whether hackers exploited it before the update was installed.
paragraph5: Businesses must investigate their past exposure alongside fixing their systems. According to Narayana of Mirror Security, investigators should identify which systems were exposed and review activity from before patching. This includes checking server logs, unusual system behaviour, unauthorised file changes and suspicious network connections. Organisations should also look for unexpected programs running on their servers or unexplained changes to files and configurations. Security teams can use monitoring tools to bring together information from different systems and identify patterns that may indicate an attack. Sathyanarayanan recommended reviewing activity from at least a week before the October 21 patch release, given that exploitation attempts were reported before public disclosure. Businesses should not assume that installing a fix eliminates the risk of an earlier compromise. If investigators find signs of an attack, they should preserve logs and other evidence, involve their hosting provider or an incident response specialist, and assess whether credentials need to be replaced. Patching alone may not remove malicious software or unauthorised access established before the fix. An attempted attack does not necessarily mean hackers gained access. Equally, the absence of security alerts does not guarantee that a system is safe. Timely patching must go hand in hand with continuous security monitoring, as attackers can move quickly once vulnerability details become public. The PHP2Shell disclosure demonstrates why cybersecurity cannot end with a software update. Businesses need to know what technology they run, fix vulnerabilities quickly and establish whether attackers gained access before the fix was applied.

author: TechPulse
excerpt: For years, we at Inc42 have tracked the Indian tech startup ecosystem and seen it grow from a kid to…
paragraph1: SUMMARYOver 70 Indian new-age tech companies have already crossed the IPO milestone and are now listed on the bourses The cumulative market cap of listed new-age tech companies as of now exceeds $173 Bn 15 new-age companies — AceVector, Moneyview, Rentomojo, ESDS, Purple Style Labs, Turtlemint, Klassroom, Shiprocket, LEAP India, Kissht, Aye Finance, Fractal Analytics, Amagi, Shadowfax and SEDEMAC — have made their public market debut in 2026. For years, we at Inc42 have tracked the Indian tech startup ecosystem and seen it grow from a kid to an adult. Among the clearest signs of evolution and maturity of this ecosystem is the growing number of startups eyeing a public listing now. For Indian companies, achieving a public listing has for long symbolised operational progression, transparency, and long-term viability.
paragraph2: For startups, it’s a relatively new but increasingly critical rite of passage, one that not only signals coming of age but also creates pathways for investor exits and wealth creation. Currently, a handful of startups, including the likes of Razorpay, PRISM, PhonePe, among others, are in various stages of their IPO journey. Meanwhile, over 70 Indian new-age tech companies have already crossed the milestone and are now listed on the bourses. The list also includes Indian companies like MakeMyTrip and Freshworks, which are listed on Nasdaq in the US.
paragraph3: India’s startup IPO wave reached its peak in 2025, surpassing the previous year’s momentum. While 18 startups listed in 2025, 17 startups have already reached that milestone in 2026. With companies like Cult.fit, OYO, others, eyeing to tap the public markets this year, the list is only expected to grow further this year.

bangla_paragraph1: সংক্ষিপ্তসার ৭০ টিরও বেশি ভারতীয় নতুন যুগের প্রযুক্তি কোম্পানি ইতিমধ্যেই আইপিও মাইলফলক অতিক্রম করেছে এবং এখন এক্সচেঞ্জে তালিকাভুক্ত। তালিকাভিত্তিক নতুন যুগে প্রযুক্তি কোম্পানীগুলির বাজার মূলধন এখন পর্যন্ত ১৭৩ বিলিয়ন ডলারেরও বেশি। ১৫ টি নতুন যুগ কোম্পানি  এসভেক্টর, মানিভিউ, রেনটমোজো, ইএসডিএস, পার্পল স্টাইল ল্যাবস, টার্টলমিন্ট, ক্লাসরুম, শিপ্রকেট, লিপ ইন্ডিয়া, কিশট, আই ফাইন্যান্স, ফ্রেক্টাল অ্যানালিটিক্স, আমাগি, শ্যাডোফ্যাক্স এবং সেডেম্যাক  ২০২৬ সালে তাদের পাবলিক মার্কেটে আত্মপ্রকাশ করেছে।
bangla_paragraph2: স্টার্টআপগুলির জন্য, এটি একটি অপেক্ষাকৃত নতুন তবে ক্রমবর্ধমান সমালোচনামূলক রীতি, যা কেবল বয়সের আগমনের সংকেত দেয় না বরং বিনিয়োগকারীদের প্রস্থান এবং সম্পদ সৃষ্টির পথও তৈরি করে। বর্তমানে, রেজারপে, প্রিজম, ফোনপে সহ কয়েকটি স্টার্ট আপ তাদের আইপিও যাত্রার বিভিন্ন পর্যায়ে রয়েছে। এদিকে, 70 টিরও বেশি ভারতীয় নতুন যুগের প্রযুক্তি সংস্থা ইতিমধ্যে মাইলফলক অতিক্রম করেছে এবং এখন এক্সচেঞ্জে তালিকাভুক্ত। তালিকায় মেকমাইট্রিপের মতো ভারতীয় সংস্থাগুলিও অন্তর্ভুক্ত রয়েছে।
bangla_paragraph3: ভারতের স্টার্টআপ আইপিও তরঙ্গ ২০২৫ সালে তার শীর্ষে পৌঁছেছিল, যা আগের বছরের গতিবেগকে ছাড়িয়ে গেছে। ২০২২ সালে তালিকাভুক্ত ১৮ টি স্টার্ট আপ, ২০২৬ সালে ইতিমধ্যে ১৭ টি স্টার্টার আপ এই মাইলফলকে পৌঁছেছে। কুল্ট.ফিট, ওয়ো, অন্যান্য সংস্থাগুলির সাথে এই বছর পাবলিক মার্কেটগুলিতে ট্যাপ করার লক্ষ্যে, এই তালিকাটি কেবল এই বছর আরও বাড়বে বলে আশা করা হচ্ছে।
bangla_paragraph4: ১৭ টি নতুন যুগের কোম্পানি  টনবো ইমেজিং, জেটওয়ার্ক, এসভেক্টর, মনিভিউ, রেনটমোজো, ইএসডিএস, পার্পল স্টাইল ল্যাবস, টার্টলমিন্ট, ক্লাসরুম, শিপ্রকেট, লিপ ইন্ডিয়া, কিশট, আই ফাইন্যান্স, ফ্রেক্টাল অ্যানালিটিক্স, আমাগি, শ্যাডোফ্যাক্স এবং সেডেম্যাক  ২০২৬ সালে তাদের পাবলিক মার্কেটে আত্মপ্রকাশ করেছে। এখন পর্যন্ত তালিকাভুক্ত সংস্থাগুলির মোট বাজার মূলধন ১৬৭ বিলিয়ন ডলারেরও বেশি। তালিকাভিত্তিক স্টার্টআপগুলির সমস্ত তথ্য একত্রিত করতে ইনক ৪২ ভারতীয় তালিকাভদ্ধ নিউ-এজ টেক কোম্পানি ট্র্যাকার চালু করেছে।
